characters.description: Liverpudlian bum and all-round slob, Third Technician David Lister was discovered under a pool table as a baby. He is a fairly competent man, but has a complete and utter lack of ambition and is quite happy in his slobby routine. Lister was the sole survivor of the Cadmium-2 leak which wiped out the crew ofRed Dwarf, because he was serving eighteen months' "temporal stasis without pay" for smuggling a cat onto the ship. Abusive Parents: The alternate Lister fromLast Humanwas adopted by rich parents who beat him while the main Lister chose to live with a poor family who loved him. Adaptational Attractiveness: Lister's counterpart in the unaired American pilot(s) was a tall,square-jawedHunkplayed by Craig Bierko, a man who looked like he should be playingHan Solo, not Lister. Craig Charles noted his dismay at this, as did many fans, as it removed Lister's relatability andflawsand turned him into aFlat Character. In the "Dwarfin' USA" documentary in the Series 5 DVD, he also admitted he wasn't pleased with the character'sRace Lift, but what annoyed him most of all was that, all things considered,invokedhe thought Bierko was actually quite good. In the same documentary, Danny John-Jules stated that he believed the reason for the drastic change in Lister's character wasExecutive Meddlingfrom NBC (the studio producing Red Dwarf USA) being worried that American audiences wouldn't take to a "John Belushi"-esque slob, so they made Lister a dashing "Han Solo" type. Craig Bierko himself wasa fan of the UK original, and later admitted that he believed his castingwas the reason the pilot failed, and in a 2009 interview on Kevin Pollak's Chat Show, Bierko said that casting him as Lister was a "huge mistake". characters.name: Arnold Judas Rimmer
characters.description: Lister's immediate superior, Second Technician Arnold Rimmer (B.S.C., S.S.C.) is an ambitious but unpleasant and almost universally hated underachiever. Born on Io, Rimmer was loathed by his brothers and classmates, who went on to achieve great things while he remained a lowly Second Technician. Any references to his underachievements are immediately blamed on mitigating circumstances. He includes his only two achievements after his name, B.S.C. and S.S.C. (which stand for Bronze Swimming Certificate and Silver Swimming Certificate). He steadfastly believes in the existence of aliens and attributes any unexplained events to such aliens. It was Rimmer's incompetence which led to the leak, killing him and the other crew members. Rimmer was resurrected by Holly as a hologram after Lister's stasis. Earning his highly-respected father's approval lays heavily on Rimmer's mind, and is one of the larger reasons why his self-loathing is so enormous, and yet his ego so similarly massive. Abusive Parents: When he was 14 years old, he went to court, divorced his parents and got visiting rights to the family dog every other weekend. He and his three brothers were abused by their father in various ways; the most severe of them was the use of arackto try to accelerate their growth (Rimmer's father had been refused entry to the Space Corps for being an inch below regulation height). Indeed, all of the abuse they suffered was to make them succeed where Rimmer Snr. had failed; unfortunately, Arnold continually tries to use this as aFreudian Excusefor his constant failures and annoying behaviour, whilst his brothersother than Howard at leasteach become successful in their own Space Corps specialty. In a deleted non-canon scene in Rimmerworld established that Rimmer's brothers all had mental breakdowns and caused substantial bodycounts. Accidental Hero: In "Officer Rimmer". When the crew come across a ship in mortal danger, rather than risk going into the asteroid field, Rimmer decides

characters.name: Cat
characters.description: Cat (sometimes The Cat) is the last known member ofFelis sapiens(also speltFelix sapiens), a species which evolved from the kittens of Lister's pet cat Frankenstein. Cat is known for his outlandish fashion sense, and gauges danger by how it will affect his looks. Abusive Parents: Rare justified example, the novels say the only female cat aboard when he was younger would hit him with aFrying Pan of Doomif he tried to have sex with her, so he reckoned she was probably his mother. Ace Pilot: Thanks to his superior sense of smell. Actually Pretty Funny: For all his antipathy for Rimmer, the Cat is quite happy to laugh in Lister's face when Rimmer makes a joke Cat likes at Lister’s expense. Adaptational Backstory Change: In the series and most other forms of canon, the Cat was born a feline humanoid from the start on Red Dwarf, being the descendant of Lister's cat Frankenstein from the very far future. InRed Dwarf: Titan, however, the Cat instead started out as a completely normal (if still obsessed with dancing and fashion) cat on Titan, is alive in Frankenstein's time, and was uplifted to his humanoid form via biological modification.

characters.name: Holly
characters.description: Red Dwarf's computer, Holly starts off amazingly intelligent with a purported IQ of 6,000. However, he has become senile before Lister's return to non-stasis. After an encounter with his counterpart from an alternate universe, a blonde female named Hilly, Holly performed a sex change on himself. Adaptation Name Change: Is based on a computer called Hab from the originalDave Hollins: Space Cadetradio sketches. A.I.-cronym:Titanreveals that in at least one universe, Holly's name is an acronym, standing for "HologeneratingOracularLucidLisptalkYABA". A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Averted. Although Holly is regularly a menace to the crew, it's never intentional on his part. The crew soon learn not to rely on him. Ambiguous Gender Identity: Holly intially starts as male presenting and is referred to by male pronouns, but then performs a 'head sex change operation' and becomes female presenting and is reffered to by female pronouns. However, Holly's reason for doing so is wanting to remember Hilly, not because of gender dysphoria, which doesn't mean Holly is automatically a trans woman. However, their comfort in switching could mean they are non-binary,genderfluid/bigender or something else. The fact that Holly is an A.I and so technically has no biological body so no biological sex only confuses things more. It's worth noting that this wasn't really planned out by the creators, the recasting was hastily done because Norman Lovett left the series.

characters.name: Kryten2X4B-523P
characters.description: Kryten is a 4000 series mechanoid. He was encountered by the crew on the wreck of the starshipNova 5, where he had obediently served his three female owners, not realising they had died on landing. Although, in the novels Kryten is actually the cause of the crash as he scrubs the computer's motherboard and guidance system out with hot soapy water as a nice surprise, causing it to malfunction and randomly spout French poetry. Lister helped to break Kryten's programming and he eventually chose to oppose Rimmer, before leaving on Lister's space bike. He crashed and was rebuilt by Lister, giving him a new accent and new programming. Absurdly Dedicated Worker: He's first encountered obediently serving the three female crew members of theNova 5, completely oblivious to the fact that they were killed when theNovacrash-landed. Adaptational Early Appearance: He appears at the start of the show's second season but earlier in theExpanded Universe:He joins the cast in the first novel,Infinity Welcomes Careful Driversthat was otherwise a novelization of the first season.He was already on theRed Dwarfbefore it left Earth in the American pilot. He joins the cast in the first novel,Infinity Welcomes Careful Driversthat was otherwise a novelization of the first season. He was already on theRed Dwarfbefore it left Earth in the American pilot.

characters.name: Kristine Kochanski (Alternate Universe)
characters.description: Navigation Officer Kristine Kochanski was Lister's partner, who perished along with the other crew members. Shortly after Rimmer's departure fromStarbug, the crew encountered an alternate version of themselves where Kochanski had survived the leak instead of Lister. Kochanski was saved from falling into a dimensional vortex by Lister, but the vortex closed, preventing her from rejoining her crew. Action Girl: Both Kochanskis definitely have their moments. Alive in the Alternate Universe: The Kochanski from the main universe was killed in the same radiation leak which took the lives of Rimmer and almost everyone else on Red Dwarf. This Kochanski comes from a universe in which she was put into stasis instead of Lister, thus allowing her to survive the leak. Alliterative Name:Ret Connedfrom her first name originally being Christine to Kristine. Amicable Exes: They're not stated to have had a relationship until later in the series, but Lister and the first Kochanski appeared to be this, judging by the brief scene they shared together in "The End."

characters.name: Kristine Kochanski (Original)
characters.description: Navigation Officer Kristine Kochanski was the love of Lister's life and ex-girlfriend, who perished in the radiation leak that wiped out the crew. Action Girl:In the hallucination created by the psirens, she's shown as this by "killing" attacking psirens.Her book counterpart inLast Humanis also skilled at judo and tackles a leopard-human hybrid with nothing more than her bare hands and a rubber band. In the hallucination created by the psirens, she's shown as this by "killing" attacking psirens. Her book counterpart inLast Humanis also skilled at judo and tackles a leopard-human hybrid with nothing more than her bare hands and a rubber band. Adam and Eve Plot: InLast Human,her overarching goal is to settle down with Lister, start a family... and then find a biolab that can allow them to rebuild the human race through more sophisticated methods.The novel ends with the two of them getting down to step one on the now-terraformed Rage World.

characters.name: Captain Frank Hollister
characters.description: The overweight captain ofRed Dwarfwho is killed off (along with the rest of the crew bar Lister) halfway through the first episode. Hasn't stopped him being the most frequently recurring non-main cast member. Acrofatic: When he gets spiked with Viagra in "Pete Part I", he claims he had to do a handstand on the toilet seat in order to pee. Adaptational Slimness: He's nowhere near as fat in theSmegazinecomics as he is in the show. Adaptation Name Change:Herlast name is Kirk in theInfinity Welcomes Careful Driversas a nod toStar Trek: The Original Series.She's called captain Tau in theRed Dwarf USApilot.Red Dwarf: Titangives his first name as Randolph, sinceTodhunter's first name is also Frank. Herlast name is Kirk in theInfinity Welcomes Careful Driversas a nod toStar Trek: The Original Series.

characters.name: Frank Todhunter
characters.description: Adaptation Name Change: The novels have a technician called Petrovitch fill Frank's role taking Lister to the captain and then bringing him to the stasis booth. Rimmer notably claims his name isChristopherTodhunter when he has Lister drive him to a brothel, he could possibly be impersonating a crewmember. Ambiguously Gay: Kochanski claims Todhunter was gay in her universe, something Lister finds absurd because he was married and slept around with women. It might have just been something she made up to help Lister with his claustrophobia. Not So Above It All: When Rimmer takes issue with Lister calling him a smeghead, Todhunter chimes in to confirm Rimmerisa smeghead. Reasonable Authority Figure: He is on friendly terms with Lister and tries to tell him that nobody wants to go through with putting him into stasis. He also hears out both Lister and Rimmer's side of the story when trying to establish why Rimmer has put Lister on report so many times. Throwing the Fight:Titanmentions that he plays golf badly on purpose to let Hollister win and Hollister is a terrible golfer.

characters.name: GeorgeMcIntyre
characters.description: Adaptation Expansion: His backstory is fleshed out in the book, giving him a gambling problem that causes him to commit suicide to escape his debts. All There in the Script: According to the original script for "The End",McIntyrewas killed by a radiation leak from the same drive plate that Rimmer was supposed to repair. Presumably, this was more localised before Rimmer botched the job and wiped out the rest of the crew. As You Know: The purpose of his character is to explain how hologram technology works to the audience. Captain Hollister explains thatMcIntyreis incapable of touching anything and he himself explains that Holly is only capable of generating one hologram at a time, even starting his explanation with the trope name. Attending Your Own Funeral: While he's not seen at the funeral itself, the crew throw him a welcome back party when his hologram gets switched on. He even cracks jokes about it. Dies Differently in the Adaptation: While the script says he died as a result of a radiation leak, heAte His Gunin the book due to being massively in debt toThe Mafia, who were likely going to absolutely torture him to death based on what they did to his nose.

characters.name: Olaf Petersen
characters.description: One of Lister's drinking buddies prior to the accident. Adaptational Job Change: His rank in the original series is Catering Officer, whileInfinity Welcomes Careful Driversmakes him a Third Technician andTitanhas him as a Drill Toolist, 4th Class. The Alcoholic: Petersen is perpetually drunk with him basically being in that state every night from the age of twelve. Alcohol-Induced Idiocy: InBackwards(the book, not the episode), he decides to go for a drink or two, which culminates in him hurling condoms filled with luminous green fluid at a Shore Patrol guard post and attacking one Shore Patrolman by stapling his penis to his groin. Ascended Extra: He plays a larger role in the books, particular in Rob Grant's iteration to the point that he has his own subplot inRed Dwarf: Titan.

characters.name: YvonneMcGruder
characters.description: Red Dwarf's female boxing champion, she was the one women to have sex with Rimmer during his lifetime. Action Girl: Something of anInformed Ability, as it's not shown, but Rimmer mentions that she was the ship's female boxing champion. Adaptational Job Change: A brief look at her uniform in her one appearance on the show reveals her rank as Deck Sergeant. The books alternate between Flight Technician and Geo-Mapper, although it's possible she became the latter after she transferred off the ship. The Ghost: Her only actual appearance occurs within theBetter Than Lifetotal immersion game. Otherwise, she's just referenced. Love Interest: For all his cynicism about love, it's implied Rimmer was really into her and that he may have had a pre-existing crush on her before they had sex.

characters.name: The Skutters
characters.description: The maintenance robots of theRed Dwarf, and frequently serving as Rimmer's hands before his hard-light upgrade (much to their displeasure). A.I. Is a Crapshoot: One of the skutters goes mad from computer senility and rewires the entire ship's electronics in "Bodyswap". Other than that, usually averted. Cowboys and Indians: A pastime of theirs is to play Cowboys and Indians. Cute Machines: For service robots, they're surprisingly cute. Death by Adaptation:Better Than Lifefeatures almost the entirety of the Skutters being accidentally wiped out by Rimmer's clumsy attempt to startRed Dwarf'sengines so they can avoid the black hole.

characters.name: Talkie Toaster
characters.description: A very minor, but very well-remembered, character, Talkie Toaster belongs to Lister, is equipped with artificial intelligence and, to the annoyance of everyone, completely obsessed with making toast. Was destroyed off-screen by Lister sometime during the first two series and rebuilt (with a completely different voice and appearance) by Kryten in Series IV. It's not clear if Talkie Toaster is defective, or if it's just because the product is so cheap (₤19.99, plus tax). Way too cheap. And way too nasty. Adaptational Badass: He kills a Polymorph inBetter Than Life. Adaptational Jerkass: InBetter Than Life. His introductory chapter states that if his offers of toast are refused enough times, he starts throwing out bitter recriminations and tirades of verbal abuse in extremely coarse language. After using what the super-intelligent Holly told him to help the ship escape a black hole, he becomes insufferably arrogant, talking down to and insulting Kryten nonstop. All There in the Manual: It is explained inBetter Than Lifethat Lister bought Talkie Toaster because it annoyed Rimmer. It even expands on how obsessed Talkie Toaster is with toast, starting with friendly requests and moving on to demands, screaming fits, begging, and obscene language that will make a pimp blush, and how it will wake you up repeatedly in the middle of the night offering toast. It will use extortion, guilt trips, and veiled threats to have you eating buttered delights. Do you want some toast? You'd better. Arch-Enemy: Lister considers Talkie to be his nemesis in his Series XII appearance.

characters.name: Ace Rimmer (What a guy!)
characters.description: Pandimensional super-hero, Ace Rimmer is Rimmer's counterpart from another dimension. Ace was held back at school, which spurred him on to succeed. Any non-Rimmer character may remark 'what a guy!' upon meeting Ace. The Ace: Turned up to eleven. He is in many ways a parody of the trope, being aComically Invincible Herowho can do everything and has all the ladies (and guys) swooning over him. Ace Pilot: Starts out as a test pilot for the Space Corps. Alive in the Alternate Universe: The main universe version of Rimmer died after failing to fix a drive plate properly on Red Dwarf and being exposed to lethal levels of radiation as a result. As such, it is a sign that this version of Rimmer is a better person than him that he is still alive. That said, he does end up killed by a Neutron Tank in Dimension 165, but he still survived longer. Back for the Finale: Was supposed to come back to save the crew in the alternate ending for Season Eight. Although this wasn't the finale, the show did go off the air for eleven years.

characters.name: Hudzen  10
characters.description: An android who arrives as Kryten's replacement. Unfortunately, the time spent alone on his journey has taken its toll on his sanity. Ascended Extra: The Hudzen 10s are only mentioned in one episode but become a playable race inRed Dwarf – The Roleplaying Game Ax-Crazy: After millions of years alone, Hudzen is homicidal and relentless. Dissonant Serenity: He begins singing a lullaby while advancing menacingly towards the crew while pumping his shotgun. Forgotten Phlebotinum: The shuttle he arrived in is presumably still docked on boardRed Dwarfbut has never been mentioned since. Possibly no more useful than the Starbugs and Blue Midgets and likely only needed to be large enough for him and his bag of guns.

characters.name: Nirvanah Crane
characters.description: A brilliant and beautiful hologram serving aboard the holoshipEnlightenment. Despite coming from a culture that disdains emotional attachment, especially when it comes to sex, she and Rimmer fall in love with each other. All There in the Manual: Her backstory was revealed in an interview on the officialRed Dwarfwebsite: She was born in 2482, and worked on Triton. In the early 2500s, whilst conducting tests on diminishing nuclear fallout, some scientists inadvertently blew up part of Pluto while Crane was on it. Crane was resurrected as a hologram and, as one of the greatest geniuses in the Solar System, was posted to the Holoship. Beehive Hairdo: Her hair is in a noticeably high style. Defrosting Ice Queen: Initially she's polite enough but not emotionally invested, hailing from a cultural milieu that has done away with emotional attachments to family and friends andregards sex as guilt-free pleasure and exercise. She's visibly confused about her developing feelings for Rimmer that begin to shift from sympathy to love to the point where she's willing to sacrifice herself to let him fulfill his dream — something the rest of the crew of theEnlightenmentfind incomprehensible. Ethical Slut: A trait she shares with the rest of her crew. Sex is simply a matter of recreation to her, and she casually offers to sleep with Rimmer shortly after they met.Nirvanah:We are holograms. There is no risk of disease or pregnancy. That is why in our society we only believe in sex — constant, guilt-free…sex.

characters.name: The Inquisitor
characters.description: An extremely powerful simulant who, according to legend, survived to the end of time itself. Concluding that there was no God or afterlife, and that the only purpose of existence is to lead a worthwhile life, he embarks on a mission to judge everyone who has ever lived. Those he deems to have wasted the gift of life are erased from existence, and replaced with people who weren't fortunate enough to be conceived. Unsurprisingly, this includes numerous members of theRed Dwarfcrew. Ax-Crazy: By virtue of being asimulant. Catchphrase: "Justify yourself." Demonic Possession: He communicates through Lister when the crew are onStarbug. The Dreaded: Kryten is terrified of him. Rimmer and Cat soon follow.

characters.name: Mr. Flibble
characters.description: Another minor character who has achieved surprising fame despite his lack of screen time, Mr Flibble is a penguin hand puppet used by Rimmer when under the influence of a holovirus. Is known for his capacity to become very cross. Ascended Extra: Like the Toaster, he does interviews on the series' website. Ax-Crazy: He wanted to dosomethingto the Boyz so hideously violent that even an insane Rimmer was taken aback. It would apparently have made a mess. Consulting Mister Puppet: He's theFormer Trope Namerand the current page image. Eye Beams: Like Rimmer, he can fire "hex vision" out of his eyes (despite being a puppet). It is possible he is a hologram puppet.

characters.name: Dwayne Dibbley
characters.description: The Cat's dorky alter ego, he first appeared in "Back To Reality" and then showed up in various ways over the years, including theCan't Smeg, Won't Smegspecial. Alliterative Name:DwayneDibbley. Even the sound of it is dorky. Ascended Extra: He started out as The Cat's polar opposite for "Back To Reality" who had played the AR simulation game as The Cat to play someone cool. He was so popular with fans that he was brought back as The Cat minus his cool in "Emohawk: Polymorph II", a disguise he wears in "Back In The Red" and as Rimmer's cooking partner in the "Can't Smeg, Won't Smeg" special after Cat himself refused to team up with Rimmer. Black and Nerdy: He's this way partly as a counterpoint to the cool of The Cat and partly becauseRed Dwarf's creative team felt that this trope wasn't common enough. British Teeth: According to The Cat, they could be used by druids as a place of worship.

characters.name: Legion
characters.description: A gestalt entity that imprisons the Dwarfers on his station. Made up of their combined intellects, he requires company to be anything but a mindless essence. Affably Evil: While he is the main antagonist of the episode he appears in, it can't be said that he's not a great host. He gives Rimmer aHard Lightdrive, removes Lister's appendix to cure his peritonitis and gives each of the crewquarters suited to their personalitiesas well as feeding them top-notch food. Lister notes that, when he writes his "Good Psycho Guide", he is going to give Legion raves with a rating of four-and-a-half chainsaws. All Your Powers Combined: When several people are around him and conscious, he gains all their memories, personalities and abilities. Every one of these is magnified, making the whole greater than the sum of its parts. When a group is reduced to one conscious person, he simply becomes that person, something Kryten uses to defeat him. Be Careful What You Wish For: As the scientists who created him died, he felt it, eventually being reduced to a "swirling essence",able to do nothing more than roam about the halls of his station, waiting to be again. Then, after a day with the Boyz, he admits returning to that state feels like a promotion. Composite Character:In-Universe. He is a combination of everyone who is on board his research station. When he started out, he was composed of the most brilliant minds of the 23rd century. As a result, he created artistic masterpieces and technological wonders, such as theHard Lightdrive. When they died, he became nothing until the Dwarfers arrived. Krytenabuses thisto reduce Legion to being just him, which forces Legion to obey Kryten's programming and preserve the lives of the crew over his own.

characters.name: Epideme
characters.description: A virus that Lister becomes infected with. Created as a rival to the nicotine patch, it instead kills its victims. It's actually sentient and the crew patch in the universal translator to try and reason with it. Affably Evil: Sure, he's a virus, but he is willing to communicate with the crew, even filling in gaps in Kryten's knowledge.Epideme:C'mon, you've caught a virus. It's fatal, it happens. Doesn't mean we can't be friends. Body Surf: When Epideme kills his victim, he takes control of their body and infects a new victim, removing all trace of himself from his original host. Didn't Think This Through: He's quick to take the opportunity to infect Kochanski via her hand (actually the hand of his previous victim), never considering that she would remove the limb right then and there in order to stop him from spreading further. From a Single Cell: When Kryten and Kochanski force him into Lister's right arm and cut it off, seven percent of his cells are still there and begin to multiply again, which delays Lister's death by just under and hour.

characters.name: Warden Ackerman
characters.description: The sadistic warden of the Tank, he sets out to make life hell for the Dwarfers during their two-year stint. All There in the Manual: We learn a lot about his backstory inan interview with the Talkie Toasteron theRed Dwarfwebsite, such as how he once worked on the prison ship from "Justice". Bald of Evil: He's bald and is the closest the series has ever had to a recurring antagonist. Blatant Lies: He claims to the captain that he's "extremely nice" and "lovely". Butt-Monkey: He's been the victim of several pranks by inmates, such as having his glass eye stolen, beingdosedwithTruth Serumandanti-impotence drugsand having his quarters vandalised. To stress how much this trope applies, in most of these casesRimmerwas involved.

characters.name: Kill Crazy
characters.description: A prisoner inRed Dwarf's brig who volunteers for the Canaries and accompanies the main characters on several suicide missions. He's quite unstable and longs for some action. All There in the Manual: His real name, according to the official website, is Oswald Blenkinsop. Even his Canaries uniformlists him as Kill Crazy. Ax-Crazy: It's even in his name. Being cooped up in the Tank has done no favours for his sanity. Blood Knight: He and Baxter deliberately sabotage Lister and Rimmer's efforts to use the time wand so they can fight the T-Rex. Fiery Redhead: His red hair matches his violent temperament.

characters.name: Baxter
characters.description: The Bully: To the other inmates in the brig, particularly the Dwarfers. The Dreaded: Rimmer claims that grizzly bears run screaming from Baxter. Fat Bastard: Very fat and a prison bully. Gargle Blaster: Rimmer describes his prison hooch as being "about 300% proof". And that's not much of an exaggeration, as Lister and Rimmer are extremely drunk on it after a small sip. Lethally Stupid: He and Kill-Crazy intend to fight the T-Rex barehanded, under the warped belief that the T-Rex's short arms will give them the advantage.

characters.name: Pree
characters.description: A computer salvaged by the crew from a derelict, which they install aboardRed Dwarfto replace Holly. She has predictive functionality, which allows her to predict what the crew would do and perform that task without needing to consult them. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Her predictive function allows her to anticipate what her ship's crew would do in any given situation and perform the task as such. Unfortunately, since the crew are so incompetent, she basically screws up jobs for them before they get the chance to do it themselves.Lister manages to exploit this and gets her to delete herself. Buxom Beauty Standard: We don't get to see, since she appears as a head and shoulders onscreen, but Rimmer orders Kryten to install large breasts on her. Graceful Loser: When Lister makes an argument that the crew would delete Pree to preserve their lives and the ship, she deletes herself with a simple "Your logic is faultless". Mission Control Is Off Its Meds: She basically takes over the ship and runs it as incompetently as the regular crew but with far more efficient incompetence than they could possibly manage on their own. She also evicts Lister into the vacuum of space when he resigns from the crew and loses his oxygen privileges as a result and then setsRed Dwarfon a collision course with the nearest star in a mission she calls "Operation Sizzle".

characters.name: Hogey The Roguey
characters.description: Affably Evil: The main reason he seems to be trailing the Dwarfers is because of sheerboredom, and the Dwarfers themselves are not threatened by his presence whatsoever. Canon Immigrant: Of sorts. He was originally meant to be a character in the ill-fated movie, and ended up inThe Beginningthanks to it being partially based on an early draft of the film script. Catchphrase:"Joo keeledz my bruzzer!""I challenge you to a duel across time and space!" "Joo keeledz my bruzzer!" "I challenge you to a duel across time and space!"

characters.name: Butler
characters.description: Butler is a Series 3000 mechanoid who served on board the Nova 5, who the Dwarfers go to meet in the hope that it will help Kryten with dealing with his mid-life crisis. However, instead of being a typical mechanoid like Kryten was when he joined the crew, Butler proves to be far more. Always Someone Better: He's this to Kryten (despite being a less advanced model). He's an artist, scientist and writer who broke his programming on his own, speaks languages better than Kryten and is loved by everyone, includingtheUniverseitself who he has on speed dial. Foil: To Kryten, being the same model but created earlier. They both suffered the loss of their crew and were therefore forced to evolve beyond their programming, the difference is that Butler did far more than Kryten ever did.

characters.name: Aniter
characters.description: The M-Corp AI whose purpose is to sell M-Corp products to people, whether they want them or not. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Her only purpose is to sell products by any means necessary. In doing so, she will cause Lister pain, start fires, cut off his ability to speak, and drain his life. Freemium: She offers users a free trial weekend and then locks basic features, such as the ability to speak, behind a paywall. Hoist by Their Own Petard: Kryten defeats her by purchasing a virus from her that deletes her immediately. The Unblinking: She does not blink, which makes her more unsettling.

characters.name: Rodon
characters.description: Big Bad: Main antagonist of "The Promised Land". Cain and Abel:He's The Cat's older brotherand is the antagonist of "The Promised Land". Cats Are Mean: He's the leader of theFelis Sapiensat the time of "The Promised Land". He also rules over them with an iron fist, tries to eliminate the Dwarfers and forces the other members of his species to worship him. Cold-Blooded Torture: He inflicts this on Brother Sol by scratching at his back with his claws. Cruel and Unusual Death:He gets torn apart by his own subjects when Rimmer projects a laser pointer onto his chest.

characters.name: Saunders
characters.description: Bemoaning the New Body: Saunders doesnotlike being a hologram, from the inability to touch anything solid, to the loss of everything that made his life worth living when he was alive. Butt-Monkey: Every moment of Saunder's time in the novel seems to involve him suffering in some way. First, he gets killed. Then, he has to put up with the bureaucracy of being a hologram.Thenhe loses his wife, the deeds to his house, his bank account, and everything he owns. Then he's not even allowed shore leave. Then he accidentally smacks himself in the balls in a moment of frustration. Then he's subjected to an infuriating time being condescended to by an extremely obtuse psychiatrist. Finally, when GeorgeMcIntyreshoots himself to avoid gambling debts, Saunders is finally switched off to make way for a higher-ranking hologram, which frankly comes as something of a relief. Death Seeker: Though he's not suicidal and wouldn't be able to commit suicide if he was, Saunders is greatly looking forward to the prospect of being switched off. As such, he's very happy when the death ofMcIntyreleaves him out of a job. Groin Attack: He tries to smash his fist on a table, but because he's a hologram, it passes through and hits him in the groin. Unwanted Revival: Saunders reflects that he'd have been happier if he'd been left dead, even if an afterlife didn't exist.

characters.name: Petrovich
characters.description: Affably Evil: Handsome, charming, and popular, he even reminds Rimmer that he has an exam when Rimmer has forgotten. Oh, and he's smuggling illegal game sets for profit that are potentially deadly to users. Always Someone Better: He's this to Rimmer. He's handsome, popular, heads up A-Shift, which gets all the best work, and has already passed his Astronavs. Naturally, Rimmer is extremely resentful of him. The Rival: Rimmer's opposite number in A-Shift, Rimmer despises him, mostly because he has everything Rimmer wants. Venturous Smuggler: Rumours abound that he's secretly a drug dealer, something Rimmer does his best to spread. It turns out that he really is a smuggler, and ferryingBetter Than Lifeheadsets to Triton to sell to bored terraformers with a value estimated at the equivalent of ten years' wages. And this version of the game is far more hazardous to the player than its original TV show incarnation in that it hides itself from the player's memory, which will kill them slowly as a result. Up Through the Ranks: He's already passed his Astronavigation exam when the story begins and is just waiting on his promotion.

characters.name: Juanita Chicata
characters.description: Allegorical Character: Juanita as a whole represents two very negative aspects of Rimmer's personality, namely his problematic attitude towards women, and his own self-loathing. Awful Wedded Life: Her sole purpose in the game is to make Rimmer's life miserable, either by destroying his property, having affairs with dozens of employees, or just refusing to let Rimmer sleep with her. Cheating with the Milkman: Has been conducting a series of affairs with just about every male employee at Rimmer's business, including several couriers who were just there to drop off a package. Hair-Trigger Temper: Prone to falling into destructive tantrums over the tiniest of things. Even minor annoyances, like the telephone being dirty, or there being nothing on television she wants to watch, end up costing Rimmer millions in damages. Hope Spot: After the divorce, Juanita gets personality surgery and Rimmer finds himself falling in love with her all over again, to the point that he decides to run away with her so they can be happy in a new life. Unfortunately, the bank picks this moment to repossess Rimmer's body, and Juanita doesn't have the money to save him because she blew all of it on a shopping trip.

characters.name: The Jittermans
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: Jimmy is easily the most violent and aggressive of the inmates of the soundwave prison, and even more inclined to get into shootouts with the cops than Tonto. Cop Killer: Both of them are very casually about killing police officers; in one scene, Rimmer in Trixie's body can only watch in horror as Jimmy in Rimmer's body shoots two cops and cripples a third. Grand Theft Me: Jimmy is initially just Rimmer's cellmate in the soundwave prison, but after it turns out that Jimmy's body has been auctioned off, Jimmy claims Rimmer's body as his own - leaving Rimmer trapped in the body of prostitute TrixieLaBouche. Horror Hippies: Tonto is a hippie and a firm believer in bringing down the establishment through spree-killing and criminal mayhem - to the point that he even has hand-painted flowers on his revolver. As it turns out, this is because he's actually a character from a craptacular pulp novel about evil hippies that Rimmer read when he was younger. Politically Incorrect Villain: Once Rimmer winds up in Trixie's body, the Jittermans prove themselves to be extremely misogynistic, treating him with sexist insults at best and physical abuse at worst, eventually forcing him into prostitution to pay their bills.

characters.name: M'Aiden Ty-One
characters.description: Alcohol-Induced Idiocy: He's not as much of a drunk as a Chi'Panastee, but M'Aiden has a nasty habit of using scramble cards to get buzzy, a serious mistake when surrounded by Agonoids that want to kill him for spare parts.His scramble card habit leads to his undoing, when D'Juhn Keep tricks him into using one that shuts down his body. And I Must Scream:Djuhn'Keep tricks M'Aiden into using a scramble card that he is told will increase his reaction time and enhance his pleasure nodes. In reality, the card actually contains a computer virus which begins shutting down M'Aiden's systems one by one. He starts off as confused and disorientated and gradually grows weaker until he is unable to move or even speak properly. The absolute last thing the virus goes after is his pain receptors, so he is fully conscious and can feel everything as D'Juhn harvests him for the replacement parts he needs to get himself back in full working order. Decoy Protagonist: Villainous variant. M'Aiden looks to be the best-placed to be the main villain and permanent POV character for the Agonoids.By his third chapter, he's infected with the Armageddon Virus by Djuhn'Keep and dismantled for parts. Cruel and Unusual Death:Infected with a mind-destroying virus, subject to the ultimate humiliation in being left helpless, before being dismantled while still alive and still fully capable of feeling pain. Eye Scream:He's last seen getting one of his eyeballs levered out with a tyre iron by Djuhn'Keep. Ironically, he had just replaced said eye by taking it from another Agonoid after losing his original when mugged while drunk.

characters.name: Djuhn'Keep
characters.description: Big Bad:The true villain ofBackwards,the biggest threat to the Boys from the Dwarf, indirectly responsible for the death of Ace Rimmer, and (via the Armageddon virus) Rimmer and Kryten. Can't Kill You, Still Need You: The only reason why he hasn't been dismantled for parts is due to his capacity for invention and design keeping the Agonoid fleet going through the centuries. But it's noted that it's only a matter of time before too much of him breaks down to be useful, whereupon he will be nothing but spare parts and scrap metal. The Chessmaster: Of all the Agonoids, he's the most ruthless and cunning. His capacity for invention has him create the Wheel Of Death, a race between all of the Agonoids to a central hub where the winner will torture Lister to death. His creation of the Apocalypse virus and tricking of M'Aiden Ty-One into infecting himself allows him to rebuild his ruined body, whereupon he manages to lure the rest of the Agonoids to the Hub of Pain for its grand opening and crush most of them to death by cranking up the gravity. Conducting the Carnage:When he betrays his fellow Agonoids by forcing them into the trap-laden corridors meant for the Dwarfers, he turns up the volume on the speakers and waves his fingers in the air to the sound of their screams of agony, "as if he were conducting the sweetest of sweet symphonies". Cruel Mercy:He goes out of his way to spare M'Aiden Ty-One until the last minute so he can endure every moment of his torturous dismantlement.Upon cornering the Boys from the Dwarf, Djuhn takes great delight in telling them that they aren't going to die for averylong time, to the point that he goes out of his way to resuscitate Lister and get him into a spacesuit when Starbug finally runs out of oxygen.

characters.name: The Snugiraffe
characters.description: Brown Note Being: A creature so sickeningly repulsive that no-one can look at it without vomiting (save for holograms and mechanoids, who have to resort to retching). The Snugiraffe is well aware of how it looks and doesn't care. Its creator(s) at least has the decency to be a little embarrassed. Covered in Gunge: It's said to look as if someone's just thrown a bucket of mucus all over it. Mind Prison: Is directly in charge of a virtual reality prison designed to torture the inmates by sealing them in a world based on everything they hate. Mix-and-Match Critters: Part snake, part slug, part giraffe. An Offer You Can't Refuse: After a few months in Cyberia, the Snugiraffe and a representative of the Reco Program drag an inmate out of their virtual world with an offer: participate in their experiments and enjoy some time with a Symbi-Morph before the inevitableSuicide Mission, or be sent back to Cyberhell for the rest of their sentence. Most inmates pick the former option - including Lister.

characters.name: Reketrebn
characters.description: Actual Pacifist: Though its shapeshifting powers would make it a formidable combatant, Reketrebn never harms anyone, instead using its powers solely to make itself difficult to damage or coerce. This is presumably part of its training, given that disloyal Symbi-Morphs helped the Simulants take over theMayflowerin the distant past and the GELF State didn't want the same thing to happen to them. Because You Were Nice to Me: One of the reasons why Reketrebn ends up preferring Lister over Deki is because Lister actually treats it as a friend rather than a slave, sharing meals with it, giving it the use of its bed, and even lying to the jailers to spare it punishment. As such, once it's given full understanding of Lister's pain, it's not long before Reketrebn helps him escape. Drama-Preserving Handicap: If Reketrebn were capable of harming people with its powers, it would be a threat on par with the Polymorph. As such, when aiding Lister, it can only use its powers for disguise, armour, and escape. A Form You Are Comfortable With: Subverted. When it's bonded with Lister and her conditioning takes hold, Reketrebn takes on Kochanski's form to try and please him, at first completely naked and then dressed in a ballroom gown, only for Lister to politely turn it down. When it takes Rimmer's form, he also brushes it off. After this, Reketrebn takes on itsShapeshifter Default Form, which makes Lister more at ease. Friendship Moment: After being encouraged to relax in itsShapeshifter Default Form, Reketrebn and Lister share a quiet dinner together, forming the basis of a real friendship between the two.

characters.name: MichaelMcGruder
characters.description: The Ageless: Genetically altered so that he doesn't age, making him technically immortal - unlike theGELFs, who are merely extremely long-lived. As such, it's likely he's biologically just as old as the GELF State itself. Boxed Crook: After the GELF mutiny and an indeterminate period of time as a slave of the newly formed GELF State, he ended up as a prisoner on Cyberia; then, much like Lister, he was offered a chance at a reprieve by taking part in the GELF State's efforts to colonize a planet that could save them from the apocalyptic plunge into the Omni-Zone. Unfortunately, this left him and two thousand other convicts on the receiving end of the Rage with no way of escaping; by the time Lister and Reketrebn are sent in, Michael's team has been reduced to a few dozen desperate survivors. Broken Pedestal: Yvonne brought up Michael to believe that Rimmer was an officer and a hero, resulting in Michael taking the same path in life, achieving very real military victories and getting himself assigned to a one-way colonization mission into deep space, all because he believed that it was what his father would have done under the circumstances. As such, Michael is not at all amused when he actually meets Rimmer and realizes that the whole thing was a lie; not only is he left overwhelmed with depression, but he's evenmoredisappointed when Rimmer freezes up when pitted againstthe Other Listerfor the first time and gets both of them captured. Colonel Badass: A Lieutenant Colonel in the Space Corps Marines, Michael fought on Hyperion during the Saturn War. The Comically Serious: He's usually the most serious person in the room, so he tends to look amusingly out-of-place compared to the eccentricities of others. This is most drawn attention to in his opening scene, in which he remains stubbornly formal and continuously peppers his speech with "sir", even in the face of the President's borderline hysteria and the ongoing presence of the Longmans.

characters.name: The Rage
characters.description: Gone Horribly Right: The GELF State wanted to make a gestalt to terraform a planet to get through the Omni-zone. Their first effort was to use criminals, resulting in a malevolent deity. Second time around, they decided to use people who they falsely accused, which fixed the first problem... and left an entity formed out of sheerangerat the injustice done to them, lashing out at anyone and anything it sees. Hate Plague: Its primary mode of attack is to simply sweep over any organic life-forms in its path and infect them with its own overpowering rage, usually resulting in them killing each other in brutal melees. The only way to endure this effect is for the afflicted individuals to form a circle and ritualistically drive the Rage to focus all its power on a single target, resulting in the victim being instantly disintegrated.

characters.name: Carzon
characters.description: Suspiciously Similar Substitute: As an earlier model fromDivaDroid, he shares many personality traits with Kryten,especially once the Kryten chip is installed in his system.

characters.name: In General
characters.description: Adaptational Backstory Change:In the series, theGELFsencountered are often experimental creations that have gone horribly wrong - or the descendants of them - with the odd functional creation like the PleasureGELFsthrown into the mix. However, inBetter Than Life,they all started out as part of a genetically engineeredFantastic Underclassof custom-made athletes and living appliances - with their current descendants having degenerated into the Polymorphs over centuries of mutation and adaptation.InLast Human,GELFswere created specifically to help colonize distant planets, being engineered to be eitherexpendable, resilient, or to occupy some useful niche in colonial culture - like the Symbi-Morph sex-slaves, for example. In the series, theGELFsencountered are often experimental creations that have gone horribly wrong - or the descendants of them - with the odd functional creation like the PleasureGELFsthrown into the mix. However, inBetter Than Life,they all started out as part of a genetically engineeredFantastic Underclassof custom-made athletes and living appliances - with their current descendants having degenerated into the Polymorphs over centuries of mutation and adaptation. InLast Human,GELFswere created specifically to help colonize distant planets, being engineered to be eitherexpendable, resilient, or to occupy some useful niche in colonial culture - like the Symbi-Morph sex-slaves, for example. Body Horror: Especially so in the bookBetter Than Life, which talks about cars made out of flesh and fleshy blobs designed to win sporting matches. Crippling Over Specialization: Many of them were created for very specific tasks, particularly the athletes and home appliances. For example, Scotland fielded a goalkeeper at the 2224 World Cup that was just a massive oblong of flesh that blocked the entire goal.

characters.name: Polymorph/Emohawk
characters.description: In spite of their madness, Kinitawowi have managed to partially domesticate these creatures, creating a bird-like variant called the Emohawk. On top of their preexisting ability to remove emotions (apparently a commodity amongst the Kinitawowi), they can suck out aspects of one's personality, as Rimmer and the Cat find out. Abstract Eater: They largely subsist from emotions. Emohawks take it further by eating personality aspects as well. Adaptational Backstory Change: Whilst the TV series positions the Polymorph as specifically engineered by humans for the purposes of war, the books have them as the descendants of thoseGELFs left behind on Garbage World, their talents coming about thanks to having to survive the conditions of aDeath World. Bioweapon Beast: In the TV series, they were engineered as the perfect weapon for war, but proved to be too insane to be put to any use. Bizarre Alien Reproduction: Female Polymorphs seduce a host of a different species and lay their eggs inside them. The gender of the host doesn't seem to matter, asThe Cat is the one we see impregnated. The mother also tends to die once this happens.

characters.name: Pleasure GELF
characters.description: Aliens Speaking English: One of the few types ofGELFs to speak in English, although unlike the later appearance of theBEGGs, this is not commented on. Appearance Is in the Eye of the Beholder: They appear differently to each person, which can be confusing when it needs to converse with an entire group of them. Blessed with Suck: They can become anybody's greatest sexual and romantic fantasy... which, of course, means nobody respects you for being you. It also causes confusion when dealing with groups of people, as it appears and converses differently to everyone. Plus, with the power turned off, they look like a hideousBlob Monster. Blob Monster: Their real appearance resembles a large pile of snot. Non-Human Non-Binary: Being androgynous, they don't actually have any genders, although Camille uses female pronouns and Hector male.

characters.name: Despair/Hope Squid
characters.description: Bizarre Sexual Dimorphism: The effects of the ink vary depending on the sex - if it's a female, it induces pleasure, whilst a male will induce despair. Driven to Suicide: The general fate of anyone squirted with the ink of a male, killing themselves out of despair. Even animals do it. Gone Horribly Wrong: They came about as an attempt at creating life on an ocean planet. It worked all right, but it led to a creature that spread destruction wherever it went. Hallucinations: Their ink induces hallucinations of either joy or despair as a defense tactic. "The Reason You Suck" Speech: Andy, an agent of the despair squid's toxin, gives a comically low appraisal to the Dwarfers when they think they're waking up from a four year VR campaign. Naturally, Rimmer gets it the worst. It's likely there is a guy like Andy that appears to depreciate all victims of the toxin.

characters.name: Psirens
characters.description: Big Creepy-Crawlies: Giant cockroach-like monsters which suck out brains. Brain Food: They usually suck out the brains of any victims who fail to evade them. They even have a slurpy straw to do so. Hoist by His Own Petard: They create illusions by reading their prey's mind. This can backfire on them in multiple ways:When a Psiren poses as Kryten, it gives itself away bycalling Lister "Dave", no doubt picking up on Lister's desire for Kryten to consider him an equal.Another Psiren trying to fake out the crew by claiming to be Lister is caught out when the two are instructed to play the guitar. In reading Lister's mind, the Psiren gains his delusion that he isnotaDreadful Musician, playing the guitar with great skill (which of course leads to the Cat and Kryten blasting it). When a Psiren poses as Kryten, it gives itself away bycalling Lister "Dave", no doubt picking up on Lister's desire for Kryten to consider him an equal. Another Psiren trying to fake out the crew by claiming to be Lister is caught out when the two are instructed to play the guitar. In reading Lister's mind, the Psiren gains his delusion that he isnotaDreadful Musician, playing the guitar with great skill (which of course leads to the Cat and Kryten blasting it).

characters.name: Kinitawowi
characters.description: All There in the Manual: The website provides an explanation for how they appeared in deep space - they were considered genetic waste and sent off to space due to their abundance of mucus. They were told that they were to become great space explorers to get them to agree to this. Attack Hello: If they're feeling friendly, they fire an arrow at you. If they'renotfeeling friendly, they skin you alive and turn you into a beanbag. Bonding Over Dislikes: They're on friendly terms with Simulants over their mutual hatred of their human creators to the point that the rogue simulant in "Beyond A Joke" has a Kinatowowi partner. Dumb Muscle: They're not exactly smart, but it's not exactly a good idea to piss them off, or they will kill without remorse. Global Currency Exception: InLast Human, they are the one breed of GELF that doesn't use sperm as currency. Unfortunately, Lister discovers this the hard way and offends the tribe's chief.

characters.name: Biologically Engineered Garbage Gobblers (BEGGs)
characters.description: Aliens Speaking English: They are capable of speaking English, with the explanation given that they were taught it by a person who went to English school before going on to consume the poor guy. Extreme Omnivore: Being designed to consume garbage, they are capable of eating "sediment, sludge and slop", although this leaves them permanently drunk. This proves to be their undoing when they all die thanks to choking on the electric wires they were chewing. The Gambler: They usually participate in friendly poker games, which proves to be an issue for Lister when he gambles away Rimmer and Starbug. I'm a Humanitarian: They are perfectly willing to consume the occasional human, as one person who went to an English Boarding School found out. Low Culture, High Tech: They have a groinal exploder in spite of their otherwise basic culture, which they had recovered from theERRAstation.

characters.name: The Sakenyako
characters.description: Because You Were Nice to Me: Butler was able to cure them of their "skin demons", leading them to consider him an honorary member of their tribe, make him godfather to their chief's daughter, and giving him a lifetime's supply of GELF Berry Wine. Fantastic Racism: The one specimen we see doesn't have a high opinion of humans, considering them scum. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: Their appearance is somewhere between the Kinitawowi and theBEGGs, and have a similar mix of cultural and technological aspects of the former.

characters.name: Vindaloo Beast
characters.description: Implacable Man: The beast is so tough that it's able toNo-Sellbazookoid blasts without even slowing down. Kryptonite Factor: The only thing that can kill it is lager.

characters.name: Vindaloovians
characters.description: Absolute Xenophobe: Before their policy was wiped to simply wiping out all humanity, they intended on wiping out everyone in the universe. Cyclops: They all have only one blue eye. Edible Theme Naming: Vindaloovian names sound suspiciously like curry dishes consumed by humans. The Empire: Their main government is the Great Vindaloovian Empire. Fantastic Caste System: Their society is split into three hard classes - Tarka refers to any official, answerable only to the Emperor, the skilled middle class (including military officers) carry the rank of Bindi, and the rest, consisting of soldiers and labor, belong to the Grunti rank. It is possible to rise up through the classes through deeds, although this privilege is not extended to family units.

characters.name: Nakhi Nenkas
characters.description: Alliterative Name:NakhiNenkas. The Ghost: They're discussed by the Red Dwarf crew, but they have never actually appeared on-screen. Nature Adores a Virgin: They prefer the blood of virgins over non-virgins, much to the concern of the Cat who is a virgin. Our Vampires Are Different: These vampires are genetically created creatures who dwell in deep space and hunt for virgins using pheromones and scent.

characters.name: Symbimorphs
characters.description: Composite Character: Symbimorphs are a combination of Polymorphs and PleasureGELFs, using the shape shifting abilities of the former, while having the ability to become the perfect mate of the latter. Objectshifting: Like the Polymorph, Symbimorphs can take the form of other objects, such as couches, elevators, or even dung. Psychic Link: They have a number of hooks they can insert into a host as a sort of psychic transmitter. The more hooks in a host, the stronger the link. They prefer to have all of their hooks in one person. Sex Slave: GELF society tends to view them as this, partially bonding them to prisoners who volunteer for the Reco Programme for their last night as a sort of last request to allow them to have sex with anyone they desire. Shapeshifter Default Form: Their default appearance is an androgynous black and white matrix humanoid.

characters.name: Holograms
characters.description: Android Identifier: They look identical to humans, so need the H to distinguish themselves. The tie-in novelInfinity Welcomes Careful Driversdescribes it as "the stigma of the dead". Awesome, but Impractical: With someone's brain patterns recorded, being a hologram is effectively resurrection. However, the computer runtime and power requirements to generate a hologram are astronomical, meaning that your only two options are to be either a mission critical crew member on a Space Corps vessel or very rich. Brought to You by the Letter "S": They have a giant H on their forehead to distinguish them from normal humans. That said, it is possible to remove it, as seen with the hologrammatic version of Ace Rimmer. Fantastic Racism: In the first book, it's stated that holograms are discriminated against and treated as second-class citizens because they are seen by the living as a reminder of their own mortality. Holograms often hold equal rights marches. Given the power and computer run time requirements, only the mega-rich and mission-critical Space Corps personnel are resurrected as holograms. Rimmer had once thrown a stone at one of these marches as a child and one of his early thoughts after his death is that he's now a "dirty deadie". The series briefly touches on this too, where Channel 27's employment of a hologram as a newsreader is considered progressive. Hard Light: Series 6 introduces "hard light", which allows holograms to be capable of touching things. Rimmer gets upgraded with it by Legion and later holograms such as Ace Rimmer, Katerina Bartokovsky, and Howard Rimmer are seen using the technology.

characters.name: Simulants
characters.description: Killer robots designed for a war that never took place, some escaped the dismantling program and now prowl around deep space. They have a strong hatred for humans and will torture and kill any they come across. The episode "Twentica" introduces a subspecies called "Expanoids". Unlike normal Simulants, they seek to enslave humanity. Adaptational Backstory Change: InLast Human,they're not robot soldiers, but were designed to aid human colonization efforts, built for maximum endurance and programmed to do anything to ensure their individual survival and that of the species, although Lister does buy a dozen of them to use as soldiers to assist in his assault on the Cyberia complex. Adaptational Heroism: In the RPG, a player can also choose a simulant as their character. Adaptation Name Change: They're called "Agonoids" in the novel "Backwards".

characters.name: Mechanoids
characters.description: A.I. Getting High: Holly manages to concoct a brew in "The Last Day" that gets Kryten drunk and even gives him a hangover the next morning. There's also Outrazone, a drug that Able is addicted to that gives him a high, but also drastically reduces his intelligence over time. Barbie Doll Anatomy: Series 4000 mechanoids don't have genitals, something which gets Kryten classified as a woman. Apparently averted for mechs assigned to the Italian starship with the reasoning that they fit in better if they could stand around cupping themselves like their human crewmates. Eating Machine:Series 4000 robots like Kryten don'tneedto eat, but Kryten is seen consuming food on a handful of occasions, notably telepathic wine in the episode "Legion" and consuming a boiled egg as part of his comedy act in the episode "Backwards". This is subtly explained by the episode "Polymorph", which reveals that the Series 4000 have an internal garbage bag inside of their torso as part of their vacuum attachment, and this is connected to their mouth, as shown when Kryten sucks up a penny and then spits it out. Thus, the Series 4000 don't actually eat, but instead fake the act by swallowing food and storing it in the garbage back. This is reinforced in the novel "Better Than Life", where mention is made of Kryten needing to change his stomach-bag to cope with the amount of toast that Talkie Toaster is forcing them to eat before it will tell them how to escape a black hole. However, the episode "The Last Day" does feature Holly and Rimmer knocking up a "mechanoid menu" of toxic chemicals and radioactive isotopes, suggesting that particular fuel sources can have a similar effect on Series 4000s as food on organic beings.It's implied that Series 3000 robots may have had a similar capacity to at least fake eating food, since Kryten makes no mention of Lister's ability to consume food being abnormal whilst they are in the reality bubble that makes them all believe Lister is a Series 3000 in the episod

characters.name: Felis Sapiens
characters.description: Achilles' Heel: Due to their enhanced senses and superior reflexes, they have an advantage over humans. However, it's very easy to distract them with a laser pointer. Adaptation Expansion: The first novel expands a lot on their species, their evolution and their nature. All Hail the Great God Mickey!: They consider Lister to be their god and have had Holy Wars based around how he was going to set up his fast food business. Bizarre Alien Biology: According to Cat's medical exam in series VIII, they have colored organs, a heartbeat that sounds cooler than a human's, and a decorated stomach wall. Cat Folk: They're descended from a single female cat and show traits of their feline ancestors, including cat flap doors, and eating meat from tins.
